react_vs_plan_execute: In this mock, ReAct takes 5 model calls for S1, 3 for S5 and 2 for S6 because each observation is returned to the model before the next action. That adds prompt/observation tokens compared with a plan-and-execute design that asks for a complete tool sequence once and replans only after an error. However, ReAct can inspect NOT_FOUND, cancelled status, delivery time and calculated refund before choosing the next tool, whereas a fixed plan risks attempting an invalid action or needs a replan. For refunds I would choose ReAct: the extra calls are justified by conditional decisions and the ability to stop safely before an unauthorized or incorrect payment.
